title: Level 4 (Expert) - D-7
notes:
West leads the ♦Q against 2♠. West's diamond opening lead wins the first trick (there is no reason to play dummy's ♦K). West switches to the ♠Q to East's ♠A. East returns a trump and South should win the ♠K as West is likely to have the ♠J given East's play of the ♠A.

It appears that the defense will be able to prevent South from ruffing a heart loser in dummy and that the contract depends on South playing the club suit for no losers. Assuming West was dealt the ♠J, South can guarantee the contract on a dummy reversal without having to guess the clubs. South should take a first round club finesse, not caring if East wins the ♣Q.

East will return a heart and South should win the ♥A. South should cross to the dummy in clubs in order to ruff a diamond in the closed hand. South should then play another club to dummy (it would not help the defense for West to ruff at any point) and ruff another diamond. South should cross a third time in clubs (he must be careful with the club spots to make this possible) and ruff dummy's last diamond to complete the dummy reversal.

If West discards (or follows), he allows South to win his 8th trick. If West overruffs South at any point, South will be able to ruff a heart in the dummy at the end. A dummy reversal is characterized by ruffing tricks in the long trump hand in an effort to establish the short trump hand.
